notes:
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: stoa-owq35.4 (multi-domain envelope enforcement — need to verify relay_queue always produces single-domain envelopes; if so .4 is documentation not a bug). Uncertainty driven by: did not read relay_queue.rs or server.rs startup path in detail; could not verify whether AppState wires MtaStsEnforcer at all. Would raise confidence if: checked relay_queue.rs envelope construction and verified MtaStsEnforcer is actually passed (not None) in production main.rs.
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — P0 CRLF bug (owq35.1) could silently prevent remote MTAs from applying our MTA-STS policy, defeating its purpose. P1 DNS dead-code (owq35.2) means transient failures produce no log, making diagnosability hard. No security-critical vulnerabilities found.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — No unsafe code in scope. Ownership patterns are sound. Error handling uses ? throughout with no unwrap() in production paths. Main idiomatic gaps: check_mx_against_policy &[String] vs &[impl AsRef<str>] (minor, no runtime cost); MtaStsError string-typed variants (will matter when TLSRPT needs structured classification). No clippy-class issues found.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: did not audit the axum handler trait bounds and lifetime elision in mta_sts_handler. Uncertainty driven by: session.rs REQUIRETLS MAIL FROM parsing not fully reviewed. Would raise confidence if: cargo clippy -D warnings run on only the 2xeks-touched files.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — Code is structurally sound. The main idiom gaps are a panicking constructor (MtaStsEnforcer::new), a duplicated error message prefix, a redundant OnceLock, and a per-call reqwest::Client rebuild. No unsafe, no gratuitous clones, no iterator anti-patterns.
Rust idiom confidence: 85% chance of no missed issue. Least confident flags: OnceLock-inside-LazyLock (might be intentional defense-in-depth for future code reorganization). Uncertainty driven by: session.rs was too large to read in full; only REQUIRETLS and EHLO sections were reviewed.
title: Review: MTA-STS, REQUIRETLS, and STARTTLS downgrade protection (stoa-2xeks)
